edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber II 8

source_text: Ecce tu pulcher es, dilecte mi, et decorus. Lectulus noster floridus; tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia nostra cypressina. Sponsa iam non de sua nigredine sola loquitur, sed pulchritudinem sponsi praedicat. Lectulus floridus: anima floribus virtutum strata. Cedrus et cypressus imputribilia: fides et spes et caritas.
pass_a_gloss: Behold you beautiful are, beloved my, and fair. Couch our shaded; beams of-houses our cedar, paneling our cypress...
pass_b_english: [[Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, and fair. Our couch is shaded; the beams of our houses are cedar, our paneling cypress >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:15-17]]. The Bride no longer speaks only of her own blackness, but proclaims the Bridegroom’s beauty. The shaded couch: a soul strewn with flowers of virtues. Cedar and cypress are incorruptible: faith and hope and charity.
